concepts.truth: Before a vector, a where: three axes, an origin, an agreed order (x, y, z).
A vector is a step, not a place - a direction and a length you can carry anywhere.
a + b is where you land if you walk a then b - tip to tail.
b - a is the arrow of the gap, pointing from here to there.
A scalar is a volume knob for a direction - same line, new length.
Magnitude is the arrow's length - the Pythagorean diagonal.
Divide by length and every direction gets a unit twin.
Velocity is the vector that edits position each tick.
Every bubble leaves along the vector you point.
Gravity applied each frame bends a straight launch into a parabola.
A force is a vector on a mass: F = m*a.
Sum every push into one net vector, then divide by mass.
Only the part along the motion does work: W = F*d*cos(t).
Friction is a constant scuff against the direction of travel.
Every mass pulls every other: F = G*m1*m2/r2.
Two bodies fall around a barycenter forever.
Constant acceleration toward a centre you never reach: a = v2/r.
